title: Q2 Multi-Horizon Blueprint for Serving & Model Roster
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Blueprint to align product, engineering, and DS on a three-horizon roadmap for Hosted APIs and the model roster. The goal is to provide a pragmatic plan that balances short-term stability (latency/SLOs), mid-term cost/perf improvements (batching, quant profiles), and longer-term model curation/experimentation that feeds OKRs for Q2. Deliverables: milestone schedule, experiment grid, rollout guardrails, dependency map, and an OKR mapping table.
goals: Stabilize top-5 hosted endpoints latency under 95th percentile SLO across peak windows
Reduce per-token cost for conversational workloads by 12% through batching and quant profiles
Define model roster pruning and promotion criteria to drive predictable rotations and minimize regressions
Establish a measurable OKR mapping between roadmap initiatives and product/engineering KPIs
horizons: Horizon 1 (0-6 weeks): Hotfixes, small perf wins, canary schedule for critical endpoints
Horizon 2 (6-12 weeks): Targeted batching + cache tuning experiments, model variant A/B for cost/quality trade-offs
Horizon 3 (12+ weeks): Model roster pruning, automated evaluation gate, and a controlled rotation cadence
milestones: 2026-02-05: Canary windows scheduled for top-5 endpoints (engineering + SRE sign-off)
2026-02-25: Mid-horizon batching prototype validated against latency SLOs
2026-03-15: Model roster criteria doc and pruning proposal shared for exec review
acceptance_criteria: Experiment grid with owners and success metrics documented
Canary schedule published with rollback criteria and playbooks
Cost/latency baseline and post-experiment measurements for at least two workloads
Model roster criteria doc approved by product + ML leadership
risks_mitigations: Risk: Canary regressions cause customer-facing latency spikes -> Mitigation: Short canary windows, automated fallback to stable variant, SLO alert throttling
Risk: Batching introduces tail latency for small requests -> Mitigation: Per-route max-batch-size and latency SLO-aware routing policy
Risk: Model pruning surprises customers -> Mitigation: Gradual deprecation cadence, communication plan, migration tooling and example prompts
notes: We will prioritize endpoints with highest cost-per-request and most variable latency distribution
Cross-functional experiment gate requires sign-off from SRE and Applied ML before any roster rotation
Budget for Dedicated capacity spikes will be reserved during peak canaries to avoid noisy neighbors
